mechanism_narrative: The unemployment rate (UNRATE) is a positive signal for the next 20 trading days, as a lower unemployment rate indicates a stronger labor market and supports corporate earnings growth.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in < 40% of instances when UNRATE < 5.0%, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is < 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year increase in the CPI index above 3.0% signals persistent inflation, prompting the Federal Reserve to tighten monetary policy, which leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 5d returns in < 40% of instances where CPIAUCSL YoY change > 3.0%, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is < 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 0.2 percentage points over 3 months and a decline in industrial production (INDPRO) below 1.0% over 3 months signals an emerging economic slowdown, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE rises > 0.2pp in 3 months AND INDPRO falls > 1.0% in 3 months
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20d returns in < 40% of instances where UNRATE rises > 0.2pp in 3 months AND INDPRO falls > 1.0% in 3 months, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is < 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: During a monetary tightening cycle (defined by FEDFUNDS > 4.5% and rising for 3 months), the Federal Reserve's policy actions lead to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days due to reduced liquidity and increased risk aversion.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60d returns in < 40% of instances during the defined monetary tightening cycle, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is < 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in housing starts (HOUST) above 1800 thousand units for 3 consecutive months signals strong consumer demand and economic expansion, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in < 40% of instances where HOUST > 1800 for 3 months, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is < 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in industrial production (INDPRO) below 1.0% and rise in residential fixed investment (RSAFS) above 1.0% over 3 months signals a supply shock in the manufacturing sector coupled with strong housing demand, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days due to inflationary pressures.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls > 1.0% in 3 months AND RSAFS rises > 1.0% in 3 months
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60d returns in < 40% of instances where INDPRO falls > 1.0% in 3 months AND RSAFS rises > 1.0% in 3 months, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is < 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A high level of the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS > 5.0%) is associated with positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days due to the market pricing in the end of the tightening cycle and anticipation of rate cuts.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 5d returns in < 40% of instances when FEDFUNDS > 5.0%, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is < 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: During a stagflation regime (defined by GDPC1 QoQ growth rate < 0% and CPIAUCSL YoY change > 3.0%), the combination of slowing economic growth and high inflation leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days due to reduced corporate profit margins and increased risk aversion.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 QoQ growth rate < 0% AND CPIAUCSL YoY change > 3.0%
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60d returns in < 40% of instances during the defined stagflation regime, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is < 0.03.
